findings.title: Google Meet fallback crashes when there is no destination calendar
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields `undefined` when the event has no destination calendar, which is common. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining. Whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType`, this throws a TypeError and the booking creation path fails. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`; use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` here.

findings.title: Video references no longer store credentialId
findings.body: This line was changed from `isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId` to `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Video results now get `credentialId: undefined` in the booking references they create. `handleCancelBooking` only deletes the video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, so newly created video meetings (Zoom, Daily, etc.) will never be deleted on cancel. Updates that look up video credentials by reference will break too.

findings.title: Org slug assignment logic inverted (unrelated change)
findings.body: The original code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, which sets the slug immediately only when billing is disabled. The new code `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` does the reverse. With billing enabled, the slug is now reserved before payment. Without billing, organizations are created with no slug at all. This change has nothing to do with the PR's purpose and silently breaks organization creation.

findings.title: Collective hosts' calendars dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null`. The later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then does nothing. In that case the other collective hosts' destination calendars are silently discarded, which is exactly the multi-host scenario this PR is meant to fix. Initialize the array (e.g. to `[]`) before pushing.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses an undefined calendarId
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` is now `undefined` whenever no destination calendar matches the credential, and the insert falls back to `"primary"`. The follow-up `calendar.events.patch` still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, which is `undefined` in that case. The patch request fails, so the Meet link is never added to the event description. Use the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` value in both calls.

findings.title: Non-Google calendars always target the main host's calendar id for every host
findings.body: `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now calls `createEvent` once per destination, each time with a different host's credential. Office365 (and Lark and CalDAV) still pick `destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, which is the main host's calendar. For other hosts this either posts to a calendar id that does not exist in their account and fails, or ignores the host's chosen calendar. Only Google uses the `credentialId` to choose the right destination.

findings.title: Fallback lookup for the calendar id can never match
findings.body: In both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent`, the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. A real `externalId` will never equal a falsy value, so the lookup always returns `undefined`. In `updateEvent`, `calendarId` is then undefined and the update fails. The old behavior of falling back to the destination calendar's externalId (or `"primary"`) is lost.

findings.title: Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar event
findings.body: `updateAllCalendarEvents` now handles multiple calendar references, one per host. However, when merging into `newBookingId`, it still uses `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes only the first old calendar event. The other hosts' old calendar events remain on their calendars after a reschedule.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation repeats deletes per reference and misses other hosts
findings.body: The recurring branch now runs inside the per-reference loop, but its body does not depend on the reference. It iterates all of the organizer's credentials and deletes the first calendar reference of every updated booking. With N references, the same deletes run N times. Because it only uses `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and `.find` (one reference per booking), the other collective hosts' recurring events are never deleted.

findings.title: loadUsers dropped the organization select and changed error semantics
findings.body: The rewritten `loadUsers` no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` for dynamic users. Code that relies on the user's organization slug, such as building org booker URLs, will get undefined for dynamic group bookings. The new try/catch also converts every error, including the intentional `dynamicUserList` validation error, into a generic 500 "Unable to load users" response. This refactor is unrelated to the destination-calendar fix.
